detail: wide: Beating the Blues trial (Proudfoot et al. 2003), one row per patient with the BDI at baseline and at 2, 4, 6 and 8 months as columns (bdi.pre to bdi.8m); BeyondMLR ch. 9 open-ended exercise 3 asks to convert it to long form. A copy of HSAUR3's BtheB, excluded as wide.
Medical school admissions, one row per applicant from one college; BeyondMLR ch. 6 guided exercise 2 fits logistic regressions of Acceptance on MCAT, GPA, Sex and Apps, no grouping column.
One row per NBA team in 2017-18 with season averages; BeyondMLR ch. 6 open-ended exercise 3 models win_pct by regression, no grouping column.
One row per New York City Airbnb listing (id unique); BeyondMLR ch. 4 open-ended exercise 1 models number_of_reviews by Poisson regression with an offset for days listed, no grouping column.

One row per community of Hale County, Alabama (1871 railroad referendum); BeyondMLR ch. 6 case study fits binomial GLMs of yes votes on distance from the proposed railroad and percent Black, no grouping column.
One row per restaurant bill one waitress served; BeyondMLR ch. 1 open-ended exercise 2 asks for a regression of the tip, Day (day of the week) and Meal are design classifications, no cluster.
Harris Trust starting salaries, one row per clerical worker; BeyondMLR ch. 1 guided exercise 1 fits linear regressions of bsal on sex, seniority, education, experience and age, no grouping column.
One row per film (FiveThirtyEight Bechdel test data); BeyondMLR ch. 1 open-ended exercise 1 asks for a regression of return on investment on passing the test, no grouping column.

Birdkeeping and lung cancer case-control study (Holst et al. 1988), each case matched with two controls by age and sex, but the table has no matched-set column; BeyondMLR ch. 6 guided exercise 4 fits logistic regressions of cancer, one row per subject.

copies beyondmlr data/c_data2.csv: the same colleges in the same order with Enrollment, type, region and num_viol (as nv), plus the derived nvrate and enroll1000; BeyondMLR ch. 4 case study fits Poisson regressions of nv on type and region with an enrollment offset.

One row per college or university (campus crime statistics); BeyondMLR ch. 6 open-ended exercise 2 models the violent share of crimes by type, size and region, region a handful of exhaustive U.S. regions, no cluster.

One row per large public university (2009 burglaries); BeyondMLR ch. 4 guided exercise 5 fits Poisson regressions of burg09 with covariates and an enrollment offset. state is a location attribute shared by few universities, most states holding one, and no source treats it as a cluster.

wide: one row per Minnesota school with the mean MCA-II math score of 2008, 2009 and 2010 as columns (MathAvgScore.0 to .2); BeyondMLR ch. 9 case study gathers it into a long table and fits lmer(MathAvgScore ~ year08 + (year08|schoolid)) and its extensions there.

Horseshoe crab satellites (Brockmann 1996), one row per nesting female; BeyondMLR ch. 4 open-ended exercise 2 fits Poisson and hurdle regressions of Satellite on Width and the other traits, no grouping column.
Kentucky Derby winners, one row per year (1896-2017); BeyondMLR ch. 1 case study regresses the winning speed on year, track condition and field size, one series.

Elephant matings (Poole 1989), one row per male elephant with AGE and MATINGS; BeyondMLR ch. 4 guided exercise 2 fits Poisson regressions, no grouping column. A copy of rethinking's elephants, excluded alike.

Philippine household size survey, one row per household; BeyondMLR ch. 4 case study fits Poisson regressions of total on age, age squared, location and roof; location is five named regions entered as a fixed covariate, exhaustive classes rather than a sampled cluster.
One row per camping party (fish caught, persons, children, camper, length of stay); BeyondMLR ch. 4 open-ended exercise 4 asks for a count model, no grouping column.
One row per house sale in King County, Washington; BeyondMLR ch. 1 guided exercise 3 fits linear regressions of price or log price on square footage, no grouping column.

Moth predation (Bishop 1972): at each of seven sites a row for light and a row for dark morphs, REMOVED of PLACED; BeyondMLR ch. 6 guided exercise 3 fits binomial GLMs of DISTANCE, morph and their interaction, quasi-binomial for overdispersion. The sites carry no id and are known only by their distance from Liverpool, the documented covariate, so no column indexes them apart from it (as coordinates, besag.checks).

subset of beyondmlr data/yrbs09.sav: the ch. 6 code draws 500 students (set.seed(33)), recodes Q66, Q2, Q84 and Q81 to lose.wt, sex, sport and media, keeps complete cases and writes this file, on which the case study fits glm(lose.wt.01 ~ female + bmipct + media, family = binomial); it drops the survey's psu and stratum.
Sitting and medial temporal lobe thickness (Siddarth et al. 2018), one row per adult; BeyondMLR ch. 1 guided exercise 2 fits linear regressions of MTL on sitting, log MET and age, no grouping column.

Weekend drinks of students in an introductory statistics course on a dry campus; BeyondMLR ch. 4 case study fits a ZIP model, zeroinfl(drinks ~ off.campus + sex | firstYear), both indicators derived from dorm. dorm names the campus's residence halls plus off campus, an exhaustive set the model reduces to fixed indicators, not a sampled cluster.

The item covariates of embrace_elp_ldt_trial: one row per letter string (word or matched nonword, paired by pairno) with isword, wrdlen and orthographic and bigram measures, which Embrace Uncertainty (largescaledesigned.qmd, LDT_accuracy.qmd) joins into the trial table on item; MixedModelsDatasets.jl's docs call it a covariate table rather than a modelling table. It holds no trial outcome and no model fits on it.
The child-level columns of embrace_fggk21 (Child, School, Cohort, Sex, age), one row per child; no page loads it and it holds no score.
The score columns of embrace_fggk21 (Child, Test, score), one row per child and test; no page loads it, and fggk21 holds the same scores with the child covariates and zScore.

MovieLens movies (GroupLens), one row per movie with its genres and nrtngs, its number of ratings; the GroupLens README's usage license says the user may not redistribute the data without separate permission, which is why Embrace Uncertainty downloads it from grouplens.org. A per-movie attribute table of embrace_ratings besides; no model fits on it.

MovieLens ratings (GroupLens): the GroupLens README's usage license says the user may not redistribute the data without separate permission, which is why Embrace Uncertainty (largescaleobserved.qmd) downloads them from grouplens.org; the pinned file is a copy on OSF. Documented model: rating ~ 1 + (1 | userId) + (1 | movieId), users and movies incompletely crossed, fitted on subsets with at least mc ratings per movie and uc per user (e.g. mvm50u80); rating holds ten half-star levels, fitted as Gaussian.

Fit records of the ratings model, one row per pair of cut-offs on ratings per movie (mc) and per user (uc) with the trimmed table's size, the model's memory size, iterations and fit time (Embrace Uncertainty, largescaleobserved.qmd); output of fits on embrace_ratings, not data.
